title: Generalized Hilbert operators on Hardy spaces
summary: Let $g\in H(\mathbb D)$, the generalized Hilbert operator $\mathcal H_g$ is defined by \[ \mathcal H_g(f)(z)=\int_0^1 f(t)g'(tz)dt,\ \ z\in \mathbb D\, \ \ f \in H(\mathbb D). \] Let $\mathcal R_p=\mathcal H(H^p)$ be the range of the classical Hilbert operator on Hardy space, equipped with the pullback norm, and let $(\mathcal R_p,H^p)$ denote the Hadamard multiplier space. For $1 2$, we prove that the multiplier space $(\mathcal R_p,H^p)$ is strictly contained in $H\left(p,\infty,\frac1{p'}\right)$. This shows that \(g\in Λ(p,1/p)\) does not imply that $\mathcal H_g$ is bounded on \(H^p\),…
